description: baseline

Target the launch-bound serialized cuSOLVER geqr2 (77.9% of baseline) across the small/medium regime n in {32,176,352,512} (7 of 12 benchmark shapes). Write a custom CUDA C++ batched blocked Householder QR: one threadblock per matrix, stage ONLY the active column panel (e.g. 512x32, ~64KB) plus the WY/T reflector factors in shared memory while the trailing submatrix stays in global; do panel factorization and WY trailing update on-chip with no per-matrix kernel relaunch; emit compact (H,tau). Pure FP32 to lock the orthogonality/residual gates first. Route every other n to torch.geqrf.

Custom batched blocked Householder QR (FP32), one threadblock/matrix, panel(32) in shared, geqr2 + WY/T + trailing update from global in column-tiles(32). Compact (H,tau). Routes n not in {32,176,352,512} to geqrf. Full validate + all 3 guards CLEAN. n=512 ~103ms vs ~980ms baseline (9.5x); geomean 47329 vs 117514 (2.48x). Profile: kernel=43.8% (102ms/640 mats), rest is eval recheck overhead.

Warp-shuffle block reduction replaces tree reduction (2 barriers vs log2(nt)). Helps small/medium where geqr2 dominates (n=32 461us, n=176 2971, n=352 8735); n=512 ~110ms (slight regression, trailing-update bound not reduction bound). Validate+guards CLEAN. Geomean 45233 vs 47329.

Tuned NB=16/nt=512 (swept NB{8,16,24,32,48}xnt{128..1024}; NB=16/nt=512 optimal). Higher occupancy: warps-active 16.7->33.3%, SM 5.9->17%, still latency-bound (DRAM 1.4%, 0.4 inst/cyc). n=512 ~39ms (was 110ms; baseline 980ms=25x); n=176 1643us, n=352 5427us, n=32 252us (now beats baseline). Validate+guards CLEAN. Geomean 27547 vs 45233 (4.27x baseline).

Pointer-hoisted trailing update (per-row base ptr into global C vs per-element addr), TN y-register-tile templated. Swept TN{1,2,4,8}: TN=1 best (34.5us vs 38.9 at parent); TN>1 regresses (y-bound mask divergence + reg pressure, occupancy-bound). Also recorded a discarded experiment: staging the C-tile in shared regressed n=512 to ~48ms (occupancy loss to 1 block/SM outweighs fewer global reads; kernel is latency/occupancy-bound not bandwidth-bound, DRAM 1.4%). Validate+guards CLEAN. n=512 ~34-36ms; geomean 26594 vs 27547 (4.42x baseline).

Warp-parallel WY/T factor build: each warp owns disjoint i-dots (V_i^T V_j) per T column, warp-shuffle reduced (was j sequential block reductions, ~120/panel for NB=16 -- big barrier source for small/medium n). Validate+guards CLEAN. n=32 103us (was 175), n=176 784 (was 1183), n=352 3297 (was 4163), n=512 ~29.5ms; geomean 21019 vs 24276 (5.59x baseline). Also recorded a discarded 4-way r-unroll of the trailing update (regressed n=512 to 45ms -- register pressure; global-load latency already hidden by 2 blocks/SM).

BRIEF DONE. HEAD=6695ba7c, geomean 21019us = 5.59x baseline (117514us). Delivered the brief's custom CUDA blocked Householder QR (FP32, one threadblock/matrix, panel(NB=16) staged column-major in shared, trailing submatrix in global, compact (H,tau)); routes n not in {32,176,352,512} to torch.geqrf (passes off-grid guard). Per-shape vs baseline: n=512 ~29.5ms (was ~980ms, 33x), n=352 3.3ms (11.8x), n=176 0.78ms (20x), n=32 0.10ms (2.85x).

WHAT WORKED (biggest levers, in order): (1) the structural rewrite itself 2.48x; (2) tuning NB=16/nt=512 for occupancy 1.7x more -- ncu showed the kernel is latency/occupancy-bound (33% warps, 2 blocks/SM capped by 32KB Vs, DRAM only 1.4%, NOT compute/bandwidth bound); (3) warp-parallelizing the two sequential-block-reduction storms -- the geqr2 reflector-apply and the WY/T (larft) build -- each collapsed j sequential block reductions into one warp-shuffle phase, together ~1.3x and especially big for small/medium n.

Lesson: the trailing-update global-load latency (ncu long-scoreboard 1.9, now the top stall) is already hidden by 2-blocks/SM occupancy, so cutting global reads at the cost of more barriers/occupancy/registers does not pay in FP32.

NEXT BRIEF (the real 16x gap to leaderboard #1 = 1293us): TENSOR CORES. n=512 at 29.5ms FP32 SIMT vs #1's ~1.3ms total => the trailing block-reflector update (C -= V (T^T (V^T C))) must run as FP16/BF16 mma on tensor cores (the field uses exactly this). STRUCTURAL DEPARTURE for the dominant n=512 b640 shapes (4/12 geomean, our ceiling at ~15ms FP32): replace the latency-bound sequential Householder panel with CholeskyQR2 + Householder RECONSTRUCTION, which is BLAS-3 (square batched GEMMs) from step 1 so tensor cores are natural. Algorithm per matrix, fully batched: (1) G=A^T A (batched GEMM/SYRK, FP32 accumulate), (2) R=chol(G), (3) Q=A R^-1 (triangular solve), (4) repeat 1-3 once on Q = CholeskyQR2 (restores orthogonality for kappa up to ~u^-1/2), (5) RECONSTRUCT exact compact (H,tau) via Modified-LU of (Q - S), S=diag(sign): the Ballard-Demmel/Yamamoto lemma — running Householder QR on orthonormal Q == ModLU(Q-S), giving Householder vectors Y into H's strict-lower, R into upper, tau/T from a triangular solve (T^-1+T^-T = Y^T Y). KEY: the factor gate ||R-Q^T A|| passes because R is regenerated from the ORTHONORMAL Q (reconstruction is stable even for ill-conditioned A), defeating why naive TF32 trailing failed (24.7>20). Run the GEMMs in TF32/BF16 with FP32 accumulation for the tensor-core win. For extreme-kappa clustered/nearrank matrices that fail chol, fall back per-matrix to shifted CholeskyQR3 (G+sigma*I) or geqrf (shape-based fallback OK, NOT content-dispatch — apply uniformly or via chol-breakdown detection). This is the likely source of the leaders' 5x edge. Keep n!=512 dispatch untouched; off-grid->geqrf. All 3 guards; report worst-case factor+orth margins on mixed/rankdef/clustered.

BRIEF-5 (CholeskyQR2 + Householder reconstruction) DONE — NO COMMIT: prototyped in PyTorch and found it is NOT viable on this host — ~3-4x SLOWER than the champion's custom Householder path, because the cuSOLVER batched Cholesky + triangular-solve serialize (only the AtA GEMM is tensor-core-fast). Champion 6dea562b unchanged (geomean 7138us, 16.46x); all prototyping was in /tmp.

THE MATH WORKS (validated the reconstruction): the key correctness insight is that you must set R = Q_h^T A directly (one GEMM, sign-agnostic) -- NOT reuse R_chol with a guessed sign diagonal. Then the factor residual R-Q_h^T A is ~0 BY CONSTRUCTION because Q_h^T A = (sign-diag) R_chol is genuinely upper-triangular when Q_h triangularizes the orthonormal Q. Householder vectors = strict-lower of L from unpivoted LU(Q-I); tau_i = 2/(v_i^T v_i) = 2/(1+||tail_i||^2) (the reflector-orthogonality condition); these reconstruct an orthonormal Q_h that passes householder_product. On well-conditioned dense n=512 (cond 2/4) and clustered, this PASSED both gates in FP32 with huge margin (scaled factor residual ~0.01-0.02 vs gate 20, orth ~0.4 vs 100) -- so the brief's gate hypothesis (reconstruction defeats the residual gate even when A is ill-conditioned, because R regenerates from orthonormal Q) is CONFIRMED for the chol-able cases.

WHY IT LOSES ON SPEED (hard measurements, n=512 b640, TF32): AtA GEMM = 1.15ms (tensor cores work!), but batched torch.linalg.cholesky(G) = 6.7ms/pass and batched solve_triangular(Q=A R^-1) = 9.2ms/pass -- both cuSOLVER batched routines that SERIALIZE (no tensor cores), the same launch-bound wall as geqrf. CholeskyQR2 = 2 passes => ~34ms + the reconstruction unpivoted-LU(Q-I) = 14ms => ~48ms total, vs the champion's full custom n=512 path at ~15ms. Even granting a free GEMM-based triangular solve, the 2x batched-Cholesky (13.4ms) + reconstruction-LU (14ms) alone = 27ms > 15ms. So the 'BLAS-3 => tensor cores natural' premise is only half-true: AtA is a GEMM (fast), but chol/TRSM/LU are factorization/solve steps that cuSOLVER serializes and that don't map to tensor cores.

ALSO: rank-deficient / nearcollinear / mixed (3 of the 4 benchmark n=512 shapes are mixed/rankdef/clustered) break chol unless EVERY pass is shifted; but shifting the refinement passes destroys the orthogonality restoration => the reconstruction's Q_h no longer triangularizes A => factor residual blows up (37-77 >> 20). So even ignoring speed, CholeskyQR cannot cleanly hold the gate on rank-deficient batches without a per-pass-decaying-shift scheme I did not find robust.

CONCLUSION: not viable as a torch-library pipeline. Realizing the tensor-core win would require CUSTOM batched tensor-core Cholesky + TRSM + unpivoted-LU kernels (multi-brief effort) -- and those factorizations are themselves sequential-per-matrix, so they'd face the same latency wall. The champion's hand-tuned Householder panel + cuBLAS bmm is already faster than the entire CholeskyQR2 pipeline. Recommend NOT pursuing CholeskyQR2 further on this batched-small-matrix regime; the validated reconstruction recipe (R=Q_h^T A, tau=2/(v^Tv), LU(Q-I)) is preserved here and in /tmp/cqr_full.py if a future custom-kernel effort wants it.
